reason: Appressed is an orientation or contact word, usually of hairs or lobes. Fused with is a union of parts. The example reads as a loose pair of different states, and the appressed grounding is doubtful. I did not look up the FLOPO definition.
Hemispherical is a shape and ± erect is a posture or orientation. These are different characters, not alternatives of one trait.
Only 'alternate' occurs in the example. Bifurcated is a spurious grounding, so there is no real 'or' pair.
Axillary is a position and congested is a density or crowding. The example is a list of two unrelated characters, and the 'on distal portion' phrase qualifies only part of it.
'Appressed-puberulous' is one compound descriptor (hairs both appressed and puberulous), not an 'or'.
The example has only 'open'. Spreading is an unsupported second grounding, so there is no alternative to record.

target: Make FLOPO_0991304 (stellate-lepidote) a subclass of PATO_0002065 (star shaped), or give both one common hair-form parent
reason: Both describe the star-shaped form of the hairs and are alternatives within that one character. They should share an attribute, so a secondary union is not needed.
'Irregular' is grounded to irregular spatial pattern, which is a wrong grounding. It should be an irregular shape. Flattened and irregular are then both shape values and belong to 07a, not 07b.
Diffuse and prominulous (of venation) are mapped to distributed and prominent. Both groundings are loose and the pair mixes distribution with prominence.

Spiral leaf arrangement is wrongly grounded to coiled, a shape. Opposite and spiral are true alternatives, but only once spiral is grounded to a phyllotaxis or placement class. They would then share an attribute (07a).
Conduplicate is a vernation or folding state. 'Expanded' is a development state, grounded loosely to dilated. They are not alternatives of one character.
Creeping is a growth habit or direction. Wiry is a stem texture or stiffness. These are different characters, so I treat it as a list of unrelated ones.
